analysis.title: DeskTalk - PAInful price action continues
key_insights: AI jitters featured heavily this week and US stocks retreated again. Risk sentiment is also dampened by Middle East escalation risk, with gold down 2% and oil up nearly 3%.
Risk appetite should stay cautious into next week's major catalysts (FOMC, BoJ), with no clear anchor for intraday markets.
Sentiment worsened after mixed tech reports overnight. NDX is down 2.5% and the Hyperscalers basket (CGUSHYPR) is down 3.2% at print.

Sector-level flight to safety: consumer staples are outperforming amid renewed strikes on Saudi Arabia and reports that the US and Israel are planning a joint military campaign against Iran after the midterms.
SPX 7658 was the downside level flagged by the futures trader and has now broken. If the break sustains into the close, further downside is warranted.

French bond weakness is the third risk-off catalyst this week. The OAT-Bund 10y spread crossed its 2011 highs, and front-end OATs fell as much as 11bp before recovering to about -4bp into the close. With no near-term catalyst, the path of least resistance is wider spreads.

Bunds outperformed, up 7bp across the curve. Eurozone consumer confidence fell further to -17.9, and Friday's PMIs are the larger focus. A turn in growth could weigh on EUR fixed income and renew contagion risk.
Citi economists note differences between France and the periphery in the 2010-12 debt crisis, but also similarities.
Treasuries outperformed on safe haven demand. Ultra bond futures (WN) are above the level to cover shorts, with today's close the official trigger, while momentum stalls at 108-16 resistance.
The desk has seen constant call buying in TY and FV, targeting 4.41% on 5s (currently 4.82%) and 4.60% on 10s (currently 5.01%).
Gilts are quietly rallying into the close. The desk sees UK fiscal risk premia as too high, but the macro strategist prefers to assess after the budget.

The USD rally is building in the NY morning. USDJPY volumes are 26% above 30-day averages, but JPY gains may be capped until FOMC and BoJ clear next week. Interest is returning in USDJPY and cross-JPY put spreads after a period of unwinds.
EURUSD breaks 1.12 at print. FX Strategy exited its short EURCHF trade at 0.903 on reaching target and remains short EURNOK, expected to benefit from geopolitical and EU risks.
